narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the total amount you requested, and the length of the loan. Your checking account status was the single most important reason for the denial. Having no checking account is relatively common among applicants, yet the model sees this as a clear signal of higher risk, pushing your prediction strongly toward bad credit. 

The amount you asked for—10,366 DM—was more than three times the average requested by people who were approved. This large sum pushed the decision further toward rejection. Finally, the 60-month duration of your requested loan is also much longer than the typical 19 months seen among approved applicants, adding additional concern in the model's assessment.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed the positive signals in your profile, such as your long employment, stable housing, and responsible credit history.

You should next focus on building a stronger checking-account history, reducing the size of future loan requests, and considering shorter repayment periods. Improving these areas will significantly raise your chances of approval on a future application. (218 words)
